scope: Twelve existing New Jersey Delaware planning records. Search-guide roles and actual itinerary failures are reviewed separately.

searchEvidence.historicProtection: No protected recovery-winner slug or protected comparison family is in this batch. Existing protected-guide tests remain required.
searchEvidence.limit: Available performance evidence does not establish demand for these individual Delaware pages. Missing rows do not prove zero demand. No Google penalty or ranking recovery is inferred from similarity or a smaller sitemap.

sources.establishes: Downstream access mileage: Poxono 26, Worthington 30, Kittatinny 34.
sources.boundary: Two former four-mile shuttle plans order those facilities upstream without an explained upstream itinerary. Do not silently reverse their identities. The table alone does not resolve current facility coordinates, entry details or a replacement trip.

sources.establishes: Lower Delaware public facility names and river-mile references. Kingwood 163.4, Fairview 162.0, Byram 156.1; the composite is 7.3 reference miles. Belvidere 198.5 and Phillipsburg 183.9 give 14.6; Bull’s Island 155.2 and Lambertville 148.6 give 6.6.
sources.boundary: These are access-list references, not surveyed track lengths or a guarantee of unobstructed passage. Fairview is a genuine primitive non-motorized access; a suspected nonexistent-access defect was not confirmed.

sources.establishes: Current manager page, dated September 29, 2026, read with the boating panel fully expanded in the browser. It lists five river launches, a Memorial Day–Labor Day permit season with Lambertville excepted, and recommends Riegelsville for the park’s Delaware River corridor.
sources.boundary: Canal lock/craft rules are not Delaware River rules. The five-launch permit statement does not establish identical conditions at other facilities. Hydrologic normal-flow percentiles are not recreational safety bands. Middle Delaware camping and numeric closure bands are not applicable simply because an endpoint source is NPS.

sources.establishes: Riegelsville is an active USGS discharge/stage station, independently checked against the official instantaneous-values response on October 20. It is downstream of the Lehigh confluence, unlike Belvidere.
sources.boundary: Six retained D&R-area plans use it as proxy context without a calibrated score or numeric cutoff. Belvidere remains the upstream launch-area station for Belvidere–Phillipsburg; the two downstream Firemen’s Eddy choices retain Trenton context. The long tidal-transition trip’s station is labeled proxy, not a direct measurement of its tidal landing.

sources.establishes: Current manager-linked one-page map, dated May 2022, downloaded and visually reviewed in full. Byram is above the Lumberville wing dam; the Bull’s Island river ramp is below it. Separate river and canal launch symbols are visible.
sources.boundary: The map does not establish a safe passage line or lawful portage through the intervening structure. The former Byram–Bull’s Island trip said to avoid wing dams without explaining how to complete the itinerary. Hold that actual passage failure rather than conceal it as a hub option. Local evidence: output/seo-release-2026-10-20/delaware-bulls-island-area.pdf.

sources.establishes: The National Wild and Scenic Rivers System distinguishes Foul Rift and the Lambertville wing dam as Class II features for experienced boaters.
sources.boundary: A general rapid class does not select a safe current passage, transfer a gauge cutoff or verify today’s conditions.

sources.establishes: The club’s own access descriptions place Lambertville’s pool upstream of its wing dam and describe complex whitewater below the opening requiring full whitewater equipment and local knowledge. It also describes Scudders as a whitewater play area.
sources.boundary: The club’s attainment/return description is not a verified public carry for the Firemen’s Eddy through-trip. No safe line or authorized portage is invented. Remaining above the wing dam cannot complete the downstream itinerary.

sources.establishes: Complete archived one-page water-trail map downloaded, rendered and visually reviewed. It locates the separate wing dams, Scudders and the Falls at Trenton, where the non-tidal trail ends.
sources.boundary: An archived map is not a current navigation clearance. The longer Firemen’s Eddy–Trenton guide requires separate rapid, tide and landing planning. Local evidence: output/seo-release-2026-10-20/delaware-water-trail-side-two.pdf.

sources.establishes: All three pages reviewed visually. The source explicitly dates its information to October 2001, lists the named facilities, warns of Lambertville’s wing-dam rapids and inadequate Trenton ramp depth at low tide.
sources.boundary: Old fees, permit details, vehicle recommendations and GPS anchors are not presented as proof of current access, surveyed water entries or current low-tide suitability.

dispositions.reason: Foul Rift Class II, a longer trip commitment and a finish before the Lehigh confluence. Correct unsupported seventeen-mile label using qualified NPS reference mileage.
Meaningful boundaries: start below Lumberville wing dam and finish before Lambertville wing dam. Byram and Firemen’s Eddy are not interchangeable substitutes.
Distinct advanced wing-dam passage. Replace contradictory instructions to remain upstream while completing a downstream trip with explicit local passage planning and no invented portage or safe line.

Scudders, Trenton Falls and tidal landing make this materially different from the Washington Crossing finish. Preserve advanced classification and add named hazard boundaries; Trenton discharge is not a tide forecast.
Short access alternative with a primitive start and separate ramp terms; repeated regional station context does not justify another guide.
Short primitive-landing alternative within the Kingwood–Byram chain; preserve its individual shuttle and landing conditions.
Retain Fairview’s genuine primitive access and a finish above the wing dam, alongside the adjacent alternatives.
Combination of the preceding two stages, not a new hazard zone. Correct 6.1 to qualified 7.3 reference miles without inventing a surveyed distance.
Preserve the shorter finish before the downstream rapid/tidal commitment, with the existing advanced classification and individual access details.
Unexplained upstream itinerary. Preserve original endpoints, IDs, sources and legacy geometry; old URL opens an explicit review explanation.
Unexplained upstream itinerary. A downstream replacement would have a different identity and requires its own review.
Intervening Lumberville wing dam without a supported passage or lawful carry. Retain research and explain the failure at the former URL.

preservation: Twelve research identities remain. Preserve coordinates, endpoint IDs, original source URLs and legacy route assets. Unrelated public records, protected guide URLs and other river families must remain unchanged. Public trip JSON and GPX exports, state/overview geometry and trip cards exclude the three held itineraries. Existing geometry-asset endpoints remain available for older-client compatibility; their availability is not a published trip or a verified itinerary.
publication: Implementation is not a live recovery test until the resulting PR is merged, both application paths are deployed, the active origin has the revised source and ordinary public behavior is verified.
measurement: Record retained guides, selected hub paths and held-path explanations as one stable family cohort. Assess confirmed Google recrawls/selected canonicals and comparable family/query performance when post-change data exists. Fewer sitemap URLs alone is not success.
